classification.difficultyReason: Connect source-scaffolded similarity and Pythagoras, then introduce and solve the unsupplied maximal square-fit equation in a remaining triangular region; strategic modelling beyond a routine scale.

content.prompt: Attic space in a particular house has the shape of a triangular prism. Triangle $AFC$ is isosceles with $AF=AC=4\text{ m}$ and $FC=3\text{ m}$. A box in the form of a rectangular prism is placed in the attic, touching both sides. A cross-section is shown in the diagram, where the face $EGBD$ of the box is shown. The box is $204\text{ cm}$ wide; that is, $ED=GB=204\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Actual2Dcrosssection of atticprism, isoscelesAFC, rectangularEGBDtouchessides, XmidpointFC, complete givens retained in editabletext. No3Dcamera or invisible faces inferred.

spec.answerVisibility: Original givens only; no answer values added.

answer.worked: Since $GB\parallel FC$, $\triangle AGB\sim\triangle AFC$. Use consistent centimetres: $AC=400$ and $FC=300$. Therefore $\frac{AB}{400}=\frac{GB}{FC}=\frac{204}{300}$, so $AB=272\text{ cm}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the length of AX, where X is the midpoint of FC.

answer.worked: In the right triangle AXC, $XC=150\text{ cm}$ and $AC=400\text{ cm}$. Thus $AX=\sqrt{400^2-150^2}=\sqrt{137500}=50\sqrt{55}\text{ cm}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the height, EG, of the box.

answer.worked: The upper triangle AGB has height $(\frac{204}{300})AX=34\sqrt{55}\text{ cm}$. The box height is therefore $EG=AX-34\sqrt{55}=16\sqrt{55}\text{ cm}$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: A box in the shape of a cube is to be placed on top of this box. Find the length, correct to the nearest cm, of an edge of the largest cube that could fit.

answer.worked: The space above the box is an isosceles triangle with base $204\text{ cm}$ and height $h=34\sqrt{55}\text{ cm}$. Let the cube edge be $s$ cm and centre its square cross-section on the box. At height s above the box, similarity gives the available width $\frac{204(h-s)}{h}$. The largest square fits when this equals its width s. Thus $s=\frac{204(h-s)}{h}$, so $s(h+204)=204h$ and $$s=\frac{204\cdot34\sqrt{55}}{204+34\sqrt{55}}\approx112.76\text{ cm}.$$ Any sideways displacement reduces the smaller side clearance, so the centred fit is maximal. To the nearest centimetre the edge is $113\text{ cm}$.
